extracted.intended_audience: American writers, poets, critics, and aspiring men and women of letters
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for producing a native, democratic New World literature — poetry, prose, drama — grounded in American character, nature, and moral purpose rather than imported aristocratic or sensational models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic portrayal of working women with dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: Portray women who work (seamstresses, housekeepers, tradeswomen, wives of mechanics) as preserving personal dignity, independence, character, and feminine charm despite practical, coarse, or mechanical occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples supplied: a seamstress who supports herself, keeps independence, aids family, and attains mental improvement; a woman carrying on a mechanical business who holds her own with carpenters and farmers yet retains womanly charm; the wife of a mechanic who makes domestic duties 'illustrious'. Anti-patterns: imported sentimentalized models (Ophelias, court-princess types) that deny the real, practical dignity of such women. Use concrete detail of work, health, character, and everyday happiness to make portraits believable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject imported aristocratic/feudal character types
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not recognize or copy character types grown of oriental, feudal, or ecclesiastical worlds as the highest standards for American personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead recast types appropriate to democratic, modern, western life: ordinary virtuous, industrious, cheerful, resolute persons of modest worldly status. Anti-patterns: full-dress, ultramarine formulas of culture, imported literary clichés, and courtly idealizations that do not fit American scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend perennial elements with new democratic combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept perennial (classical/cultural) elements but successfully adjust and recombine them into forms appropriate to modern democratic America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for synthesis: preserve what is valuable in tradition while reorganizing it to serve the needs and occasions of American cities and agricultural regions. The objective is not rejection of culture but supervision and reapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce original national archetypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Create original archetypal figures and forms that vitalize the nation's contributions and give permanent literary meaning to political/material achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great literature issues from a nation's archetypes (like Homer, Dante, Shakespeare); American letters need analogous native archetypes to give form and perpetuity to the country's experience. Anti-pattern: many facts and events remain ephemeral unless embodied in archetypal literary forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize originality over mere volume of readable print
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between the abundance of readable print (journals, novels, periodicals) and true literature: quantity does not equal literary quality or a national literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nation may circulate oceans of readable print and still lack 'literature' if it lacks original, enduring works. Beware conflating market success, erudition, or polish with genuinely formative literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw on autochthonic/native materials and idioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the nation's native scenes, characters, idioms, songs, and local life — boatmen, miners, farmers, mechanics, western speakers, regional repartee — as the foundation for genuinely American literary expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The spirit and form of literature depend on association, identity, place. Examples: local slang, stumpspeech, Maine woods, California miner, Kentucky repartee. Anti-pattern: wholesale importation of London/Paris models and second-hand fashions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place democratic self-esteem at literature's center
rubrics_metrics.description: American poetry and prose should express the divine pride and self-esteem of man, not poems that humiliate or deferentially bend before 'superiors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone should be erect and self-affirming. The new literature ought to champion democratic faith in humanity and present confident, self-respecting voices rather than servile or sentimental ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce bold, modern, kosmical poetry engaged with science
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry must be bold, modern, all-surrounding (kosmical), not ignoring science or modern life, and should look toward the future more than the past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extricate from greatest past models while remaining courteous; let science and modernity inspire poetic vision. Anti-pattern: clinging slavishly to past forms or subject matter at expense of present materials and scientific outlook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test literature by character, not just erudition or elegance
rubrics_metrics.description: The true test of high literature is the depth of character it expresses, rather than mere learning, elegance, or technical polish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character, spiritual purpose, and moral qualities should be central. Works that amuse or titillate but lack character satisfy only shallow tastes and will not endure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor cheerful simplicity and faith over morbid sophistication
rubrics_metrics.description: Great writers will be marked by cheerful simplicity, adherence to natural standards, limitless faith in God, reverence, and the absence of morbid sophistry, doubt, ennui, or burlesque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid covert, lurid, maleficent themes inherited from Puritan gloom, or fashion-driven affectations. Tone and moral posture matter: literature should uplift and manifest healthy simplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for moral civilization as literature's highest end
rubrics_metrics.description: The loftiest aim of literature is to formulate and express moral civilization — conscience, moral soundness, justice, and truth — beyond mere aesthetics or religious fervor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature should contribute to the moral development of society; the highest literary achievements will embody crystalline conscientiousness and human justice. This is presented as superior even to the highest esthetic triumphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore Nature as the pervading atmosphere and test
rubrics_metrics.description: True Nature — a restored and enlarged conception — must furnish the pervading atmosphere of poems and act as a test of all high literary and esthetic compositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature supplies esthetic, emotional, and religious elements and is central to happiness and wholesome art. Literature should be suffused with outdoor life, sky, air, water, trees, and common natural shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the full breadth of American experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature must represent the real, diverse American experience — Mississippi and Western men, Southerners, farmers, mechanics — rather than a narrow set of parlour dandies and imported sentimental types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of fresh local courage and sanity is criticized; authors should draw on contemporary national events and characters rather than repeating foreign or obsolete themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject sensationalism and market-driven averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid writing aimed primarily at sensational appetite, incident, or transient amusement — the market-driven 'mean flat average' — which produces profitable but ephemeral works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature devoted to interior and spiritual life may have smaller audiences initially but will last; do not equate commercial success with lasting literary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate the drama beyond ornament and triviality
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic presentation in America should be treated seriously and not as mere ornamental confectionery (curtains, hangings, or polite entertainments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current theatrical dribble is inadequate for the weighty needs of the nation; drama should serve substantial and patriotic purposes rather than trivial amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be open to genius arising from humble, indigenous origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that the seeds of genuine literary genius may lie in remote, coarse, or unrefined places (western idioms, local songs, miners, boatmen), and these indigenous sources should be cultivated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such rude beginnings may later sprout truly American literary flowers; do not dismiss the unpolished as unworthy of literary attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature must vitalize national life through mind and spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: The mind (imagination and intellect) must build and vitalize the permanent edifice of national meaning; literature conveys and perpetuates the highest meanings of a people's materials, politics, and achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use literature to incorporate and immortalize the nation's experiences — without such literary mediation, important events may leave no lasting record. Literature should act as the spiritual translator of material life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Envision literature as a culminating national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: After political foundations and material prosperity, literature (native expression — authors, poets, operas, architecture) is the third stage that completes national development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should see their work as part of a national project: forming a self-containing expression-spirit that democratizes and reconstructs society in alignment with American principles.
